correctness.rationale: For every real p-Banach target, leaf or barycentric extension gives universal upper bound min(2,2(n-1)^{1/p}/n). To prove sharpness choose the canonical isometric boundary map into finite-dimensional free-p space on equilateral n-set. If a proposed center has a negative affine coefficient, contractivity into the free Banach space and exact equilateral transportation norm give radius>2. For nonnegative barycentric coefficients lambda, Cúth–Raunig Theorem 2.2 minimizes over rooted spanning-tree flow costs. Each subtree flow dominates its own nonnegative lambda_j, giving lower bound 2^p sum_{j!=i}lambda_j^p; the rooted star attains it. Sorting lambda gives max_i sum_{j!=i}lambda_j^p=sum_{j=2}^n lambda_j^p on the ordered simplex. Its concavity reduces minimization to ordered simplex vertices with k equal nonzero coordinates: k^{1-p} for k<n and (n-1)n^{-p} for k=n. Minimum is min(1,(n-1)n^{-p}); strict concavity p<1 and direct p=1 analysis classify leaf/barycenter minimizers. These exact arguments cover all n>=4 and real 0<p<=1; sampled checks are only auxiliary.
